claim: html-to-text.spec.ts 'stays linear on many <style prefixes' (js/polynomial-redos) keeps the shape that replaced the one Date.now() reading per size that failed CI run 37268845925 (65 vs <64) on a PR that never touched html-to-text. The command checks exactly this. In the whole file: no it, test or describe directly followed by .skip, .only, .todo or .failing, and no call written xit(, xtest(, xdescribe(, fit(, fdescribe( or ftest( after a non-identifier character. In the test's body, from its it( line to its own closing line, after dropping // and /* */ comments: each of these as a whole line - const inputs = [250, 4000].map((n) => "<style".repeat(n)); const best = [Infinity, Infinity]; the for (let round = 0; round < 20; round++) loop head; const start = performance.now(); htmlToText(input); the best[k] = Math.min(best[k], performance.now() - start) update; const [small, large] = best; expect(large).toBeLessThan(small * 64); - plus exactly one expect(, exactly 4 occurrences of best, and none of the words return, if, while, try or Date. It is a tripwire against reverting to the old shape, not a proof the test works: it misses chained forms such as test.concurrent.only and any edit that keeps those lines but defeats them (an expect in a function never called, both sizes timing one input, a shadowed htmlToText, Math or performance); a .fit( method call or a comment naming one of the listed forms trips it. That the old /<style[^>]*>[\s\S]*?<\/style>/gi replace fails the test (ratio 239x or more against the 64x bound) is a recorded mutation result (author on Node 22; audit of PR #629, round 1, on Node 20.20.0), not re-run here. ADR 0100 review trail, 2026-10-05.
